title: Jesus Washes Their Feet
reflectionQuestion: Jesus, the greatest of all, knelt down to wash his friends' feet. What is a kind, helpful thing you could do for someone you love?
kidSafetyNotes: NEW anchor (Easter, John 13). The emotional room = LOVE KNEELS -- the embodiment of Bible PAL's whole doctrine (being held, gentle strength, the big One stooping for the small). Its own story (the foot-washing is a grace-note beat in 1850 Last Supper long; this OWNS it -- managed overlap, coat-precedent). Peter's 'You should never wash my feet!' included. Per Adam: the lesson is NOT 'you should serve people' -- it's 'the GREATEST person in the room chose to kneel' (much more powerful). Cross kept OFFSTAGE -- this is not sadness-before-goodbye; it is 'love gets down low to help.' Peter's protest -> Jesus 'this is how much I love you.' short+full, NO long (one tender scene). 'God'/'Jesus' throughout, no Yahweh. VOICE_JOHN_BELOVED (John was at this table; tender, intimate Johannine register).

scriptureKeyVerse.text: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
